title: 4/5 – Great for grinding and finishing, just wish the box was bigger
review_text: I bought the Maldon Sea Salt Flakes specifically to refill my salt grinder, and they work really well for that. The flakes aren’t as hard as those little salt pebbles I usually love, which means they dissolve into food faster—perfect when you want the seasoning to melt right in instead of sitting on top. Would be an excellent addition to the top of some homemade chocolate. The only real letdown was the size. I was surprised at how small the box is and how little salt you actually get. My brain clearly didn’t process what 250 grams looks like in practice. Once I realized I couldn’t return it, I just started using it, and I’m glad I did. It makes everything look and taste a bit fancier. Overall it’s a solid product if you like that classic flaky texture and want something that performs nicely in a grinder or as a finishing salt. Just know that with daily use the box won’t last long. Still happy with the purchase.

product_name: Maldon Salt, Sea Salt Flakes, 8.5 oz (240 g)
title: The Ultimate Finishing Salt – A True Kitchen Staple!
review_text: If you are looking to elevate your home cooking, Maldon Sea Salt Flakes are an absolute must-have. I recently picked up the 8.5 oz (240 g) box, and it has completely transformed the way I finish my dishes. The first thing you will notice is the unique texture. Unlike standard table salt or even coarse kosher salt, Maldon features these beautiful, delicate pyramid-shaped flakes. You can easily crush them between your fingers for a finer sprinkle, or leave them whole to provide a satisfying, light crunch that dissolves perfectly on the palate. What really sets this salt apart is its flavor profile. Because it is an all-natural, hand-harvested sea salt, it has a remarkably clean, bright taste without the bitter or metallic aftertaste you sometimes get from heavily processed salts. It truly enhances the natural flavors of whatever you put it on. It is incredibly versatile—I use it as a finishing salt on everything from seared steaks and roasted vegetables to fresh tomatoes, and it even works wonders sprinkled over chocolate chip cookies or caramel desserts. Knowing that it is Kosher and has been hand-harvested using traditional methods by the same family for four generations adds a wonderful layer of artisanal quality to the product. While the 8.5 oz box might seem small compared to bulk table salt, a little goes a very long way since you are primarily using it to finish dishes rather than boil pasta water. It is an affordable luxury that makes everyday meals feel gourmet. I highly recommend keeping a box on your counter!

product_name: Maldon Salt, Sea Salt Flakes, 8.5 oz (240 g)
title: Food of the Gods
review_text: I was buying a salt cellar for a friend recently, and when I did so, I tossed a box of this for myself into the cart to try, just for fun. Sure, I know more than the average bear about salt. I read a book on it, and have tried some of the fine salts, smoked salts, and I have coarse chunks of pink Himalayan salt in a grinder on my table (they look great). But, what do I use everyday for cooking? Morton Kosher Salt in a salt cellar for an easy pinch when I need it. The flakes are flat, stick to food well, do not contain the metallic-taste of iodine, readily-available, and so inexpensive, it is essentially free. I tried this salt for the first time this morning on my poached eggs. Suddenly, I understand why, long ago, salt was so valuable it was used as currency. Yes, it was a clean, clear taste, without any off-flavors. But, I expected that. What I didn't expect was the effect of the triangular crystals. They stick to the food much like the flakes, without falling off like the old-fashioned, iodine-laden crystalline cubes we all grew up with (if you have some of those still lying around, just toss them - they really aren't worth eating). But, why are they better than the Kosher flakes? Because they crunch in your mouth when you eat them. It is an almost surreal experience. I found myself looking forward to each bite, because every time I bit down, there was a satisfying soft crunch, along with a tiny little explosion of salt taste in my mouth. This salt is just fantastic! So much so that I set aside some time this evening to write a review to let people know. There are really only two drawbacks. One is it is more expensive than the Morton Kosher salt, though still extremely reasonably priced for what you get, in my opinion. The other? What the heck am I going to do with the two full boxes I still have of Morton salt now that I've found this? Very highly recommended. Get a box and try it out, even if you are skeptical. Trust me on this. Sean Logue, 2015

review_text: What makes Maldon stand out is its pure, clean flavor. The salt flakes are crisp and delicate, adding a subtle crunch and a burst of natural salinity that enhances a dish without overwhelming it. Another major benefit is the texture. Maldon’s pyramid-shaped flakes dissolve evenly and slowly. You also avoid the additives commonly found in generic salts, such as anti-caking agents or iodine. Maldon is harvested naturally and has a clean, mineral taste that feels closer to how salt should be. If you’re looking for an easy way to make everyday cooking feel more gourmet, Maldon Sea Salt is a small luxury with a huge payoff.

title: Less salty than other salts
review_text: After doing some research on the mineral content of Redmond's real salt as opposed to standard pink Himalayan sea salt, I decided to give it a try. What compelled me that the price was worth it was the simple fact that it leaves a lower carbon footprint on the globe because it is sourced closer to me than salt that comes from the Himalayas. If it was as flavorful as other salts, I would make the switch. However, it is less salty than other salts and therefore you need to use more of it, or just get used to a blander taste. If your goal is to get more electrolytes and minerals and you don't care about the salt meter, then this is a great option for you because it boasts a different set of minerals than some of the other salts out there. But if you are simply looking to switch out your standard iodized table salt for a healthier option, I would stick with the pink Himalayan. As an additive to water or homemade electrolyte drinks, it is a great product!
